text: Born Heinrich Wilhelm Schweickhardt in Hamm, he moved to The Hague, where he became a pupil of Hieronymus Lapis and started a family. In 1786 he moved to London for economic reasons and did quite well there. His daughter Katharina learned to draw and paint and became a poet. Willem Bilderdijk taught her and her sisters in London, and in 1795 they had an affair. She later married him. Schweickhardt died in London.

Kuhnert first illustrated the books of Alfred Brehm, and then went to German East Africa to watch animals in their habitat. His many paintings defined Africa for many Germans of the period. He finished a technical-commercial apprenticeship at seventeen and was a scholarship student at the Berlin University of the Arts from 1883 to 1887. From his home in Berlin he travelled to Scandinavia, Egypt, East Africa and India to make landscape and animal studies.

Van Papendrecht first studied commerce at the Amsterdam Handelsschool. At the urging of Charles Rochussen, a friend of his father's, he joined the winter programme at the Royal Academy of Fine Arts in Antwerp. After two years there he lived in Munich for four years to continue his training. In 1884 he came back to the Netherlands. He specialised in military art and also worked as an illustrator.

Mitelli was best known for quadratura, illusionistic architectural frameworks painted in fresco. He studied with Gabriello Ferrantini, called degli Occhiali, and Girolamo Curti. He worked closely for many years with Michelangelo Colonna in northern and central Italy: Colonna mainly painted the figures and Mitelli the architectural framework. His quadratura survives in Bologna, Parma, Modena, Florence and Rome. He died in Madrid while working for the court of Philip IV of Spain.

Some 19th-century art historians thought Antony van der Does came from The Hague and belonged to the Van der Does family of painters. In fact he was born in Antwerp, the son of Jan van der Does and Joanna van Orshagen, and was baptized in Antwerp Cathedral in 1609. There are no signs of a family link with the Dutch painters. He worked as an engraver and print maker in Antwerp, mainly reproducing other artists' work. He died there in 1680.

Joos de Momper the Younger was named after his grandfather, a landscape painter, and came from an artistic Antwerp family. His parents were Bartholomeus de Momper the Elder and Suzanna Halfroose. Brueghel's influence is clearly evident in many of his paintings. His work sits at the transition from late 16th-century Mannerism to the greater realism in landscape painting that developed in the early 17th century. He achieved considerable success during his lifetime.

Berlage studied architecture at the Zurich Institute of Technology and then travelled for three years through Europe. In the 1880s he formed a partnership in the Netherlands with Theodore Sanders. He is considered one of the fathers of the architecture of the Amsterdam School. His mother, Anna Catharina Bosscha, was the niece of the scientist Johannes Bosscha, who taught at the Polytechnic School in Delft. He designed an office building for the firm Kerkhoven en Co. in Amsterdam.

Born Uesugi, the son of a low-ranking samurai, Rosetsu changed his name to Nagasawa once he established himself as an artist. In 1781 he moved to Kyoto and became a student of Maruyama Ōkyo. His style was versatile, and Drinking Festival of the Eight Immortals of the Wine Cup is among his paintings. He and his wife had four children, but all of them died in childhood. Sources conflict about his family origins.

Bodenheim trained at the Rijksacademie in Amsterdam and then took lessons from the painter Jan Veth. She is known for silhouettes, most of them made for children's books, though she also made colour lithographs. Besides illustrations for books and magazines, she designed textiles, posters and book covers. She joined the Amsterdamse Joffers. Her silhouettes decorated the 1905 book Women Painters of the World.

Potthast painted people at leisure in Central Park and on the beaches of New York and New England. He started art school at the McMicken School in Cincinnati in 1870, and in 1873 he went to work at the Strobridge Lithography Company. For two years he studied under Thomas Satterwhite Noble, a retired Confederate army captain who had studied with Thomas Couture in Paris. In the Surf is among his beach studies. He is counted as an American Impressionist.

A corn chandler's son from Isleworth, Towne was apprenticed in 1752 to the London coach painter Thomas Brookshead. In 1759 he won a design prize from the Society of Arts and studied for a while at St Martin's Lane Academy. His pupil John White Abbott later said he had also studied under the court portraitist John Shackleton. His watercolour landscapes range from the Lake District to Naples and Rome. His work stayed obscure for a long time, and has been increasingly recognised since the early twentieth century.

Brady studied under Samuel Morse, who brought the daguerreotype technique to America. He opened his own studio in New York City in 1844 and photographed presidents including John Quincy Adams, Abraham Lincoln, Millard Fillmore and Martin Van Buren. When the Civil War began, his mobile studio and darkroom let him take thousands of battlefield photographs that brought home the reality of war. He is known as one of the earliest and most famous photographers in American history.

A student of Giovanni Domenico Tiepolo, Bossi was born in Trieste and worked primarily as a miniaturist in Germany, Austria, Sweden and Russia before settling in Munich. In Munich he was appointed a court painter. He also founded a collection that included a significant group of Tiepolo drawings. It passed to his daughter Maria Theresa Caroline and her husband, Carl Christian Friedrich Beyerlen, and was later sold at auction.

An engineer by training, Burton spent most of his career in Meiji era Japan, where he worked as a photographer and photography writer. His father, John Hill Burton, was a lawyer and amateur historian whose books on economics received attention in Japan. His mother's father, Dr Cosmo Innes, was one of Scotland's foremost amateur photographers. As a boy Burton was a friend of Arthur Conan Doyle, who turned to him for background for The Engineer's Thumb and dedicated The Firm of Girdlestone to him.

Stankiewicz began by studying chemistry in Kharkiv. From 1876 she studied at the Wojciech Gerson painting school in Warsaw, and from 1880 at the Académie Julian in Paris, under Tony Robert-Fleury and Jean-Paul Laurens, among others. After returning to Warsaw she regularly visited the studios of several painters, such as Miłosz Kotarbiński. She was also a graphic designer and a feminist. She received the Order of Polonia Restituta.

Jacques Stella lost his father, a Flemish-born painter, too soon to be trained by him. Jacques trained in Lyon and then spent the years from 1616 to 1621 at the court of Cosimo II de' Medici in Florence, working alongside Jacques Callot. Florentine art was a strong influence on all his work. His sister Madeleine was a sculptor, and he was the uncle of the artists Antoinette, Claudine, Françoise and Antoine Stella. He was a leading exponent of the neoclassical style of Parisian Atticism.

Bacher went to work as a decorative painter in mansions and on ships after finishing public school. In 1874 he began formal art studies with De Scott Evans, who specialised in still lifes. Shortly after, he became one of the first members of the Art Club founded by Archibald Willard. He briefly attended the Pennsylvania Academy. He is primarily known for his etchings and illustrations, and he painted oils in a variety of genres too.

The son of the engraver Carl Heinrich Rahl, Rahl attended the Academy of Fine Arts in Vienna and won a prize at nineteen. He travelled to Munich, Stuttgart and Hungary, and in 1836 to Italy. He stayed there until 1843, studying the Venetian and Roman schools in particular. His views on colour and perspective were largely formed during his years in Rome.

Delobbe was admitted to the École des Beaux-Arts at sixteen, where he was a student of Thomas Couture and William Bouguereau. His debut at the Salon in 1861 was a portrait of his mother. His original specialities were mythological, Orientalist and genre scenes in the Academic style. His career took off when he won a commission to decorate the Town Hall of the recently annexed Fifteenth Arrondissement, one of only eight such commissions given out.

From Arcisate near Milan, Bossi worked as an engraver, painter and stucco artist. Anton Raphael Mengs and Christian Wilhelm Ernst Dietrich advised him to concentrate on engraving. He stayed for a time in Nuremberg and Dresden, but he had to leave Saxony during the Seven Years' War. In 1760 he went to Parma, where the duke became his patron. He died there in 1792. Some sources misspell his name as Benigno Rossi.

Phillips learned glass painting in Birmingham under Francis Eginton. In 1790 he went to London with an introduction to Benjamin West, who found him work on the painted glass windows of St George's Chapel at Windsor. In 1791 he became a student at the Royal Academy. He specialised in portraits, and he painted many notable men of the day, including scientists, artists, writers, poets and explorers.

Piero di Cosimo is most famous for the mythological and allegorical subjects he painted in the late Quattrocento. He is said to have abandoned them and returned to religious subjects under the influence of Savonarola, the preacher who held huge sway in Florence in the 1490s and had a similar effect on Botticelli. He kept using an essentially Early Renaissance style into the sixteenth century. The High Renaissance style of the new century had little influence on him, and he kept his straightforward realism.

Hondius, a Rotterdam stonemason's son, trained under Pieter de Bloot and Cornelis Saftleven. He lived in Rotterdam until he moved to Amsterdam in 1659, and in 1666 he migrated to London, where he spent the rest of his life. Throughout his career he combined several stylistic influences and struggled to develop a style of his own. He specialised in animal pieces, and more than two-thirds of his paintings and etchings show animals.

Zonaro's father, a mason, wanted his eldest son to be a mason too, but the boy showed a great ability at drawing. With his parents' consent he enrolled first in the Technical Institute in Lendinara and then in the Cignaroli Academy in Verona, under Napoleone Nani. He is best known for realist paintings of life and history in the Ottoman Empire. Mehmet II conquering Constantinople and Fishermen Bringing in the Catch are among his pictures.

Jackson made woodcut prints after oil paintings, not in imitation of ink-and-wash drawings. He lived and worked in Paris and Venice. He produced chiaroscuro and polychrome prints, as well as wallpaper. His work was remarkable for its subtle overprinting, which brought in a wider range of colours, and for this he developed new oil-based inks. In some works he also used heavy embossing to highlight areas of the composition.

Colenbrander has been called the first Dutch industrial designer. He was born in Doesburg, where his father, one of the town's notables, worked as a commissioner, insurance agent and land agent. Besides regular school he got extra education from the local city architect. In the late 1850s he began working for the architect Eberson in Arnhem. He was also a ceramist and plaque painter.

Vaughan was indicted in 1651 for publishing a print of King Charles I, who had recently been executed, and he supported the Royalists during the English Civil War. The National Portrait Gallery calls him a versatile line engraver who produced portraits, maps, bookplates, series of prints and the occasional broadsheet. He engraved the Theatrum Chemicum Britannicum. He knew Thomas Vaughan.

The son of a well-known author, journalist and poet, Berndtson began his higher studies at the Polytechnic Institute in Helsinki. From 1869, though, he was associating with members of the Academy of Fine Arts and auditing art classes taught by Erik Johan Löfgren and others. By 1876 he had decided to be an artist, so he went to Paris to study. He was noted for his attention to realistic detail.

Dubourg was baptized in the Walloon church in 1693, the son of Jean du Bourg and Elisabeth Burlamacchi. He was a pupil of Gerard de Lairesse, Gerrit Rademaker and Jacob van Huysum. In 1718 he became sexton of a small wooden church on the Kerkstraat. When he married Eva de Kaarsgieter in 1729, he cooperated with Bernard Picart. He painted historical and academic subjects and arcadian landscapes. He was an engraver too.

Born in Broad Street, London, the eldest son of a merchant, Holloway was apprenticed at a young age to a seal engraver named Stent. He studied engraving at the Royal Academy from 1773 and exhibited pastel portraits at the Society of Artists in 1777. He became a court engraver in 1792. Later he lived in Norfolk, at Edgefield and Coltishall, where he died.

Born in Augsburg, Umbach became cabinet painter to the Bishop of Augsburg. He produced many landscapes with cattle, as well as kitchen pieces, feathered game and a few historical subjects in chiaroscuro. He also etched 230 plates of biblical and mythological scenes and landscapes. He died in Augsburg in 1693. A younger Jonas Umbach existed, but nothing is known about him except that he drew portraits.

Carreño had a painter for a father, and the father had the same name. The family moved from Avilés to Madrid in 1623, and Carreño trained there in the late 1620s as an apprentice to Pedro de las Cuevas and Bartolomé Román. Velázquez noticed him for his work in a cloister and in the Church of Our Lady of the Rosary. In 1658 he was hired as an assistant on a royal commission to paint frescoes in the Alcázar. He also painted King Charles II.

Benouville was apprenticed with his younger brother François-Léon to François-Édouard Picot and later to Léon Cogniet. He painted many landscapes near Paris, around Compiègne and Fontainebleau. He first exhibited at the Salon in 1834, and was admitted to the École des beaux-arts three years later. In 1845 he was awarded the Prix de Rome for historic landscape painting, for his Ulysses and Nausicaa. He is known for views of Italy.
